name: Southwestern Tarahumara

new_statements.quote: 5.3. Stress placement. Both modern Ralámuli and Warihio have moveable stress, in which different morphological configurations can cause primary stress to shift among stem syllables, from the stem to a suffix, or from one suffix to another, within a fixed three-syllable (from the left) stress window. The placement of stress on any particular word depends upon whether the stem or suffixes are inherently stressed and, in the case of suffixes with inherent stress, whether the stress is strong or weak (Caballero 2011b; Miller 1996:48—51, 59; Félix Armendáriz 2007:11—13).
new_statements.citation: Merrill, William L. & Don Burgess. 2014. Ralámuli kinship terminology: a diachronic perspective on diversity in the Sierra Tarahumara of northwestern Mexico. Anthropological Linguistics 56(3-4): 229-293. (Smithsonian Research Online postprint, 65 pp; DOI 10.1353/anl.2014.0010)
new_statements.locator: sec. 5.3 'Stress placement', p. 259 (p. 31 of 65); continuation p. 260: 'the Western dialect appears to be at the end of a general shift, in nouns at least, from the moveable stress pattern reconstructible for Proto-Tarawarihio to one in which stress is fixed on the stem'; p. 248-249 (sec. 5.1 cross-ref): 'The rightward shift in stress on nonidentical vowel sequences, also associated with the Western dialect'; transcription note p. 282-283 and p. 234: 'Stress is shown only on the etyma for which inherent stess can be reconstructed'.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Mirrored SI postprint (65 pp.) re-extracted with extracted text: sec. 5.3 'Stress placement' on p. 259 (the text) matches A's quote word for word; p. 260 continuation 'the Western dialect appears to be at the end of a general shift, in nouns at least, from the moveable stress pattern reconstructible for Proto-Tarawarihio to one in which stress is fixed on the stem' also verbatim. Identity: p. 231 adopts Valiñas' five areas (North, South, Central, West, Cumbre>Interior), no Southwestern/Tubares area; sec. 2 data = Rejogochi (Merrill 1977-84) and Tierra Blanca (Burgess 1991-98; refs p. 286: 'Tarahumara Baja data from Tierra Blanca, Ejido of Monterde, Municipio of Guazapares') plus Burgess 199…
new_statements.relation_note: movable stress in a left-edge three-syllable window, lexically/morphologically conditioned; Western dialect drifting to stem-fixed noun stress; nothing on tone.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ralámuli (all modern dialects) has movable, morphologically conditioned primary stress confined to a three-syllable window counted from the left edge of the word; where it falls depends on whether the stem and the suffixes carry inherent (lexical) stress and on strong vs weak stressed suffixes. Kinship reflexes show the same stress placement across dialects except in the Western dialect (Tierra Blanca), where noun stress is becoming fixed on the stem and stress shifts rightward on word-final non-identical vowel sequences.
new_statements.exceptions: Western dialect (Tierra Blanca): stress on the stem in possessed reference forms, variation in the reflex of *oýno 'father' (ono-lá), lexicalized possessed marker in ten terms (tables 15-16); rightward stress shift on final non-identical vowel sequences in Western (e.g. reflex of *bapoi).
new_statements.identity_note: OUR-BIBLIOGRAPHY WORK (listed 'likely states stress; not yet obtained', paywalled DOI), added: open SI postprint located by web search, downloaded from the the Internet Archive (direct repository.si.edu is could not be reached by automated download) and read. The stress statement (sec. 5.3) is made for 'modern Ralámuli' as a single language with five dialect areas after Valiñas 2001 (North, South, Central, West, 'Cumbre' renamed Interior; p. 231) - there is no separate 'Southwestern' area and none of the data communities (Rejogochi, Tierra Blanca, Mesa de Arturo, Aboreachi, Guachochi, Norogachi, Samachique, Huichabóachi, Balleza; Burgess 1995 five-area compilation) is in the Tubares/twr zone. Ethnologue/INALI place Tubares within the western (oeste/Baja) zone, for which the paper reports the only deviation (Tierra Blanca, Western dialect). So it covers twr only as part of a pan-Ralámuli generalization, not from twr data. | A's WORK 7 (download-failed, author unknown), added: author, pages, an open copy on the INAH's new repository, and the accent statement A could not see. Variety: 'El presente estudio es de la variante dialectal cumbre de las localidades de Samachique y Koyachique, correspondientes a los municipios de Guachochi y Batopilas, Chihuahua' (pp. 29-30) = INALI cumbres = Ethnologue Central (Samachique) Tarahumara [tar] = Glottolog cent2131; nothing from the Tubares/oeste zone. Its fn. 2 and bibliography also give a variant citation of the CET survey already held by the project ('Coordinación Estatal de la Tarahumara, Fundamentación lingüística para la estandarización de la lengua tarahumara escrita.. 1991, mecanoescrito') and cite an unpublished Caballero ms. 'The Stress System of Central Raramuri' (Choguita/Central, superseded by Caballero 2008/2011). | A's WORK 5 (not-attempted; PRIOR container 1004 had only the thesis-series list), added: a stable open repository copy, downloaded and read, and the first-hand accent statement that A's work 4 reported second-hand. Variety: 'la variante cumbres de la lengua ralámuli' of Munérachi (data also from Napáchare and Retosachi), mun. Batopilas = INALI cumbres = Ethnologue Central [tar] = cent2131; p. 78 contrasts it with 'otras variantes como la oeste y la sur (Villalpando, 2010)', so explicitly not the oeste/Tubares zone. Technical note: the PDF's roman fonts use a shifted glyph encoding (plain extracted text yields '0RUIRORJtD' for 'Morfología'); decoded per span (+29, with i/p/t/y/x = á/é/í/ó/ñ) and saved next to the PDF; the quotes are from that decoding and read as normal Spanish.

readall_conflicts: No source describing the Southwestern Tarahumara [twr] variety itself was opened, so no direct conflict exists. Two indirect signals pull different ways and are noted for the record: (a) Villalpando 2010 (held by the project, MA thesis on Turuachi; p. 27, quoting the CET 1992 dialect survey) states 'Posición del acento: Este rasgo delimita una zona OESTE que se comporta distinta en función del acento, el cual recae sobre la vocal final en la variedad OESTE, mientras que recae en la penúltima para las otras variedades' (Tabla 9: makói 'ten', sikúi 'ant' in Norte/Centro/Cumbre/Sur vs makué, sikuí in Oeste) — i.e. penultimate in the Sur area, which Caballero 2022 Table 1.2 (p. 7) and Villalpando 2010 Cuadro 2 (p. 15) equate with Ethnologue's Southwestern [twr]; but Ethnologue's own twr entry is the Tubares-area variety, not INALI's Sur (Turuachi/Chinatú), so this mapping is uncertain. (b) Caballero 2022 for Choguita (Central [tar]) describes lexically contrastive, weight-insensitive stress within an initial three-syllable window plus lexical tone. Neither statement is about twr proper; the survey's three-word 'penultimate' feature is a dialect-differentiating diagnostic, not a stress rule.

Stress is left-aligned and assigned in the first (2a), second (2b–c) or third (2d–e) syllable of the word.…

Establishes identity: alt. names Tarahumara del Suroeste, Tubare; 100 speakers (1983 SIL); location 'Chihuahua state: Tubare'; status 8a moribund; 'Typology: Nontonal'; unwritten; 'Area where extinct Tubare [tbu] language was spoken'. sources.note: Review summary (NRFH 68(1), 2020, of the volume): re-evaluates two phonological isoglosses proposed for rarámuri in the 1990s (CET 1992) — presence/absence of [g] or [k], and [i] vs [e] in unstressed syllables — as desphonologisation processes; defines three zones (occidente, centro, oriente-suroriente) for the first; concludes the two isoglosses cannot confirm the five dialect areas. Segmental / stress-conditioned vowel alternation; no tone content indicated; chapter not opened (print).
